name: Two Metal drawables, judged with the clocks held

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown: Part 1 reverted two Metal drawables because effects-cards read about 1.5x the main-thread CPU. That was judged with idle CPU clocks; waiting for a drawable idles the core, which lowers the clock, so the same work reads as more CPU time. With the clocks held two drawables should cost nothing and still save a full-window IOSurface.
measurementPlanMarkdown: Build three- and two-drawable binaries from the same source, alternate them four times with three busy processes beside them on effects-cards, scroll-div-cards, scroll-data-table, hover-grid and text-relabel (fast on), then compare missed frames and frame intervals over eight runs of three scenarios.

measurements.metric: missed frames in 24 runs (hover-grid, div-cards, text-relabel)

reportMarkdown: No CPU cost, 13-22 MB (about 9-11%) lower footprint in every scenario. Frames still arrive at 120 fps; with two drawables the main thread waits for the drawable, so the frame interval is regular (95th percentile 8.5 ms against a clustered 4.3 ms) and its maximum rises from about 7 to 9 ms. GPU time per frame is unchanged (5.8 ms on effects-cards and hover-grid).
decisionMarkdown: Keep, and flag it: this reverses the part 1 decision on corrected evidence. One line (`set_maximum_drawable_count(3)`) restores the old behaviour for an app that is GPU-bound at the frame budget.
